ai.purpose: RTT/1 engine layer for Quantum Mechanics: operator grammar, amplitude behavior, measurement, and minimal coherence examples.

engine.description: Defines the operator grammar and dimensional behavior of amplitudes, superposition, and measurement within the RTT substrate.

state_vector.description: Represents the full amplitude configuration of a system.

observable_operator.description: Defines measurable quantities and their eigenvalue spectra.

unitary_evolution.description: Describes how amplitudes evolve without measurement.

superposition.description: Represents coexistence of amplitude components prior to distinction.

commutator.description: Defines compatibility and uncertainty between observables.

eigenbasis.description: Provides the stable basis for measurement outcomes.

density_matrix.description: Represents statistical mixtures and partial coherence.

uncertainty_relation.description: Defines lower bounds on simultaneous distinctions.

dimensional_mapping.R1: Primitive amplitude behavior; unstable distinctions; coherence dominates.
dimensional_mapping.R2: Stable operator algebra; measurement structure; predictable evolution.
dimensional_mapping.R3: QM becomes a limiting case of QFT; excitation grammar takes over.
dimensional_mapping.R4: QM loses meaning; macroscopic regimes dominate.

integration.notes: RTT/1 treats QM as a coherence grammar; deeper resonance and substrate integration occur in RTT/2 and RTT/3.
